question: Why should the objective lens of an astronomical telescope have a large aperture? Give reason.

options.A: The objective must have a small aperture so that less light enters and the image is darker.
options.B: A large aperture is needed only to increase the focal length of the telescope.
options.C: A large aperture is used to reduce the speed of light inside the objective lens.
options.D: The objective collects light from distant objects. A larger aperture admits more light and therefore gives a brighter image, improving visibility of faint celestial objects.
